speeches.speaker: Bruce Billson
speeches.brief: Supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment Bill 2013, which lets regulations exempt restaurant and cafe surcharges on specific days such as weekends and public holidays from component pricing rules, noting a 2010 Productivity Commission review recommended the change and that the government has introduced 22,000 new or amended regulations while in office.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Argued that the bill would allow regulations to exempt restaurant and cafe surcharges from component-pricing requirements, reducing red tape, while criticising delays and broader costs affecting the sector.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Argued that component-pricing rules imposed unnecessary red tape on small restaurants and cafes, criticised ACCC enforcement, and supported the bill as a correction of the problem.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: Supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment Bill 2013 exempting restaurant and cafe weekend surcharges from 2009 component-pricing rules that forced venues to print two sets of menus, an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 cost per restaurant, and noted a 2010 Productivity Commission recommendation for the change, while criticising the government for introducing some 21,000 new or amended regulations against only 1,100 repealed.

speeches.speaker: Scott Ryan
speeches.brief: The opposition supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment Bill 2013, which exempts restaurants and cafes from requiring separate menus for surcharge days, implementing a Productivity Commission recommendation and reducing compliance costs estimated at $8,000–$10,000 per business. The coalition also announced a future root-and-branch review of competition law, including unfair contract provisions for small businesses.
